key_insight: Progressive Multimodal Alignment (PMA) prevents multimodal projector forgetting in continual instruction tuning by expanding expert alignment only when distribution shifts are detected, while keeping the original projector as a stable anchor.
engineering_relevance: For solid-mechanics-style multimodal pipelines, PMA offers a scalable way to preserve prior cross-modal calibration as new tasks, sensors, or loading regimes are introduced.
method: Detects multimodal distribution shifts with a lightweight representation descriptor
Progressively adds projector experts only when needed, rather than retraining a single projector
Uses an expandable router to combine expert outputs while retaining the pretrained projector as an alignment anchor
evidence_signal: The abstract reports consistent gains over prior state-of-the-art methods on two recent MCIT benchmarks, with benefits across multiple MLLM backbones.
watch_item: The added routing and expert-expansion logic may increase system complexity and require careful thresholding to avoid unnecessary growth or mis-detection of shifts.
paper_title: Progressive Multimodal Alignment for Continual Instruction Tuning
